newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese banks surge on discount to Spain sector.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese banks surge on discount to Spain sector.

text.p: Portuguese bank shares hit new highs on the Lisbon bourse on Wednesday as they traded at a discount to the Spanish banking sector, and were set to go even higher, dealers said.
Expectations of strong results in the first half on the back of recent gains in the capital markets have also influenced the latest surge in Portuguese banking shares, they added.
On average, Portuguese stocks have risen by 40 percent so far this year, while the index of financial intermediaries .BVL65 has increased by nearly 38 percent.

"The Spanish banking sector shows a price earnings ratio of nearly 20, compared with a PER of between 14.5 and 15 for Portuguese banks, and perhaps this differential explains the strong demand seen recently for the main Portuguese banks," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Since the beginning of the year, shares in Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor have risen by 49 percent to a high of 1,587 escudos, Banco Totta e Acores by 11 percent to 3,237, Banco Portugues de Investimento by 83 percent to 3,540, and Banco Espirito Santo by 52 percent to 4,150.
Shares in Banco Comercial Portugues hit a high of 3,500 escudos on June 17, a rise of 71 percent so far this year.

One analyst said: "Spanish banks have a premium over Portuguese banks because of recent investments of Spanish banks in Latin America and stakes that Spanish banks have in other groups that are producing good returns."
Analysts noted active arbitrage between Spanish and Portuguese banking stocks and said that the recent surge in Spanish banking shares had pushed up Portuguese banking stocks.
The index for Spanish banks has risen by 54 percent so far this year.
One analyst said arbitrage between Portguese and Spanish banks had intensified recently.
Analysts said share prices of Banco Pinto e Sotto Mayor and Banco Totta e Acores, both owned by businessman Antonio Champalimaud, were catching up with other Portuguese banking stocks.
"I think both BPSM and BTA have prospects to rise further. Investors are betting that they will post good second quarter results," said one analyst.
